notes: expect accepts a single name, an array (any listed answer passes), or null (= none). Distractors are frozen copies of real competing skill descriptions a typical user has installed; they compete in every case. Calibration cases assert the distractor wins, guarding against convergo over-triggering.

distractors.name: ce-plan
distractors.description: Create structured plans for multi-step work, including software and non-software tasks. Use when asked to plan, break down implementation, plan from requirements, or deepen an existing plan.

distractors.name: ce-work
distractors.description: Execute a plan or concrete work prompt end-to-end. Use when implementing from docs/plans, a spec path, or a clear build request.

distractors.name: ce-code-review
distractors.description: Structured code review for bugs, regressions, tests, and standards. Use before PRs or when asked for review.

distractors.name: ce-debug
distractors.description: Diagnosis loop for bugs and failing behavior. Use for errors, stack traces, regressions, failed tests, or stuck investigations after failed fixes.

distractors.name: ce-brainstorm
distractors.description: Explore vague or ambitious ideas into a right-sized requirements-only unified plan. Use when the user wants to brainstorm, think through scope, or decide what to build.

distractors.name: ce-commit
distractors.description: Create a git commit with a clear, value-communicating message. Use when the user asks to commit or save staged or unstaged changes.

distractors.name: review
distractors.description: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review.

distractors.name: code-review
distractors.description: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level.

distractors.name: verify
distractors.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior. Run before committing nontrivial changes.

distractors.name: spec
distractors.description: Turn vague intent into a precise, executable spec in five phases.

cases.prompt: Create a plan for issue #42: add rate limiting to the public API. Read the issue scope and the codebase first, and give every step a done-when criterion.
Implement docs/plans/rate-limit.md slice by slice with TDD and commit per slice.
Review the implementation on this branch against docs/plans/rate-limit.md and the behavior contract. Distinguish code bugs from contract gaps.
Before we start building, review docs/plans/rate-limit.md against the actual codebase: are the slices sufficient and the invariants correct?
The plan reviewer returned blocker findings on your plan. Validate the feedback and revise the plan-owned artifacts in this planner session.
The code reviewer returned two blocker findings. Validate them and repair the implementation-owned issues; stop if any is a contract gap.
Run a supervised implementation loop over docs/plans/rate-limit.md: a background worker implements, fresh code reviewers gate the exit.
Iterate a plan for this feature through supervised specialist sessions until a fresh plan reviewer passes it.
用受监督的专家会话帮我把这个规划迭代到评审通过为止。
Act as an orchestrator: coordinate planner, worker, and reviewer sessions as background agents for this feature.
Hand this plan to a background worker and watch its progress. Do not call it done until a reviewer who has never seen the code signs off with no objections.
把这个 plan 交给一个后台 worker 去实现，你负责盯进度。每轮做完找一个没看过这些代码的新 reviewer 把关，过了才算完成。
Draft the plan in a separate session and keep sending it back for revision until an independent reviewer has no remaining objections.
You supervise only: spawn separate sessions for the planning specialist and the implementer, relay results between them, and report back to me.
A reviewer just sent back three blockers on my implementation. Triage them: fix what is genuinely ours, and flag anything that is really the plan's fault instead of patching around it.
There is an approved plan at docs/plans/auth.md. Build it: write the failing test first each time, keep commits small, and do not stop until every done-when box is checked.
Someone wrote docs/plans/billing.md. Before any code is written, check it against the repo with fresh eyes: missing surfaces, wrong boundaries, steps that cannot actually be implemented as written.
Get a plan written for this feature and have it independently reviewed before we build.
Review my pull request #123.
Look over my current uncommitted diff for bugs before I commit.
Plan a marketing launch timeline for next quarter.
The tests are failing after my change. Figure out why and fix it.
Brainstorm what we should build to improve user onboarding; I have a vague idea and need to narrow the scope.
Commit these staged changes with a good message.
Turn this vague feature idea into a precise, executable spec.
Before I commit, actually run the app and confirm my change behaves correctly end to end.
Translate README.md to Chinese.
Format all files in src/ with prettier.
Summarize what changed in the last five commits.
